newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hanbo founder jailed in bribery scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hanbo founder jailed in bribery scandal.

text.p: The patriach of South Korea's scandal-ridden Hanbo Group was jailed for 15 years on Monday for bribing aides to President Kim Young-sam, top bankers and others in a case that has rocked the nation.
Chung Tae-soo was one of 10 people handed stiff prison sentences by a Seoul court in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo's failed steelmaking flagship.

The others included a former cabinet minister, three lawmakers with the ruling New Korea Party and one with the main opposition party, three ex-bankers and Chung's son, who is Hanbo's current chairman.
The elder Chung, 74, was convicted with his son, Chung Bo-keun, of bribery and embezzlement. The younger Chung was jailed for three years.
They were found guilty of siphoning off a combined 364 billion won ($408 million) from funds belonging to the country's 14th largest business group.

The bribes to bankers and politicians were to keep money rolling in to Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January under debts of five trillion won ($5.6 billion), setting off a chain of corporate failures and shaking the banking system.
The scandal shattered President Kim's credibility and unearthed other bribery scandals that led to the arrest of the president's son, Kim Hyun-chul.

A related flap over Kim Young-sam's spending on his 1992 election campaign, which opposition parties say was bankrolled in part by Hanbo, has sparked a wave of violence by students demanding the president step down.

"Your wrongdoing has caused great shock to the Korean people, harm to the country's economy and chaos in society," chief judge Son Ji-yol told the ailing Chung Tae-soo, who hobbled into court supported by a prison officer.
The court heard that Chung Tae-soo, who suffered a mild stroke after his arrest, handed out cash hidden beneath apples in wooden crates. The lawmakers admitted taking his money, but not as bribes.
"Our society should use this opportunity to break from a past where morality and reasoning were lacking and move towards a better economy and society," the judge said.

Former home affairs minister Kim Woo-suk was jailed for four years. Lawmaker Hong In-gil of the ruling New Korea Party was sentenced to seven years and his colleagues Hwang Byung-tai and Chung Jae-chull each to three years.
Another member of the National Assembly, Kwon Roh-kap, of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, was handed a five-year prison term.
Two former presidents of Korea First Bank, Sheen Kwang-shik and Rhee Chul-soo, were jailed for four years and five years respectively. The bank was the largest creditor to Hanbo Steel.
The one-time president of Chohung Bank, Woo Chan-mok, was jailed for four years.
Hanbo's former financial controller was given a 2-1/2 year jail term suspended for four years.
Chung Tae-soo has been embroiled in corruption scandals twice previously. He was convicted last year of bribing former president Roh Tae-woo, but a legal technicality spared him a jail sentence.
Monday's hearing was in the same courtroom in which Roh and his predecessor, Chun Doo Hwan, were convicted of corruption and other crimes in August last year.
